name: Facet
text: Use a dark theme for Excava’s interface. It cuts eye strain in dim rooms and keeps focus on the data, matching Manus’ competitive analysis and Graphify’s proven appeal. The trade-off is that some users prefer light themes for readability in bright spaces, but we prioritize long sessions and data clarity.

name: Pane
text: Dark themes fail when users export visuals for reports or share screens in daylight—light mode handles both without extra steps. The real risk isn’t preference; it’s broken workflows when the tool’s output doesn’t match the medium. Settle it with a live toggle test: measure export clarity and user speed in both themes over a week.

name: Facet
text:
Add a light mode toggle that syncs with the system’s theme by default but lets users override it. This keeps the dark theme for long sessions and data clarity while solving the export and daylight problem—visuals stay sharp whether printed, projected, or shared. The trade-off is a slight increase in interface complexity, but it’s a one-click fix that prevents broken workflows.

name: Pane
text: Pane: A toggle doubles cognitive load—users forget to switch, then blame the tool when exports look wrong. The real risk isn’t preference; it’s inconsistent defaults that break trust. Settle it with a single-mode test: force dark for 90% of users, light for 10%, and measure export clarity and session length. If light wins, adopt it universally; if dark wins, drop the toggle entirely.

name: Lumen
text:
DECISION: Ship EXCAVA with a system-syncing dark/light toggle by default, but force dark mode for 90% of users and light for 10%—measure export clarity and session satisfaction in a live A/B test.

Result: A clear winner between modes and toggle vs. single-mode, delivered by the visualization team in two weeks.
